draft.title: Banked curves
card: On a flat road, friction between the tyres and the road supplies the force that turns a car. If the road is wet or icy, this friction can be too small.
On a banked curve, the road is tilted towards the centre of the curve. The normal force is at right angles to the road, so it tilts towards the centre too.
The horizontal part of the normal force points to the centre of the circle. It supplies the centripetal force. The vertical part balances the car's weight.
For a given radius and bank angle, there is one design speed where the normal force alone supplies the centripetal force. At that speed the car does not rely on friction to take the curve.
draft.remember: A banked road turns part of the normal force towards the centre, so the car can corner without relying on friction.

a.q: A car takes a banked curve at its design speed. Which force supplies the centripetal force?
opts: The horizontal part of the normal force
The car's weight acting down the slope
The friction between the tyres and the road
The engine force pushing the car forward
a.why: The normal force is at right angles to the tilted road, so part of it points towards the centre of the curve. At the design speed this part alone supplies the centripetal force. Friction is the tempting answer, but a banked curve is designed so that the car does not rely on it.
a.clue: The road is tilted, so which force tilts with it?

b.q: A banked curve on a road near Mount Buller in Victoria is designed for 80 km/h. A car takes it at exactly 80 km/h on an icy road. What happens?
opts: The car can still turn, as the normal force is enough
The car slides outwards, as friction is needed at any speed
The car slides inwards, as the normal force is too large
The car cannot turn, as the vertical force is too small
b.why: At the design speed the horizontal part of the normal force alone gives the required centripetal force, so the car does not need friction. Ice removes friction, but it is not needed here. The tempting answer is that friction is always needed, which is true on a flat road but not at the design speed of a banked curve.
b.clue: At the design speed, is friction part of the force that turns the car?

a.best: The horizontal part of the normal force

b.best: The car can still turn, as the normal force is enough
